articles.title: Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang: superintelligence is arriving

facts.text: Alexandr Wang, the company’s chief AI officer and head of its Superintelligence Labs, made the case in an essay on X on Sunday.
A proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, built with Anthropic’s Claude by mathematician Levent Alpöge, was certified on Saturday by the Lean and Mathlib proof-checking communities.
The problem had resisted mathematicians since 1859.
The gaps left, he wrote, are practical ones: specific knowledge, integration work, and experimentation.
Once those close, he expects AI to overtake top humans in nearly every field, AI research included.
Wang finds it hard to imagine humans staying in charge of AI that improves itself without limit, or of a system 1,000 times smarter than they are.
The essay drew more than 8 million views in its first half day.
The 17-million-line Lean library checks out by machine, but a human-readable version of the maths does not yet exist.
US senator Bernie Sanders would go further, with a bill to ban superintelligence outright.

stories.title: Dragos planted 2 million bait prompts and caught attackers stealing from three AI hosting providers; OpenRouter drops all three

articles.title: Dragos planted 2m secrets in AI prompts and caught 3 hacked providers

facts.text: OpenRouter has removed three inference providers from its platform and stripped 125 endpoints of their Zero Data Retention (ZDR) status.
From July to November, its team sent nearly two million prompts to widely used AI services. Each one carried unique web links and working credentials, including AWS keys tied to empty accounts.
The team found attackers stealing data from three different hosting providers. The earliest breach dates back to mid-July, and none of the three knew until Dragos told them.
The findings showed no breach of OpenRouter itself, the company said.
The bait keys ended up in tens of thousands of AWS API calls.
A Chinese AI lab, which Dragos did not name, fetched the secret links from more than half of the prompts sent to its models from July to October.
That included about two-thirds of the requests marked as ZDR or “no data collection”.
“Zero Data Retention is supposed to mean something,” Moore wrote.

articles.title: China’s Z.ai launches GLM-5.4, a looped 750B model for coding

facts.text: Z.ai has released GLM-5.4, its first flagship model built on a Loop Transformer. The design runs some of the model’s layers more than once.
It said the model matches the intelligence of models with 2 to 3 trillion parameters.
GLM-5.4 runs 28 layers of the GLM-5 base model twice. That gives a deeper network with no extra parameters.
Z.ai did not publish benchmark scores for GLM-5.4 itself.
Z.ai plans to release the open weights after safety hardening.
The company named one limitation: the model tends to get caught in overly long “marathon thinking” loops.
Z.ai said a significantly larger model is coming soon.

articles.title: TikTok takes its deepfake detection tool global and adds an AI checker

facts.text: TikTok is rolling out its Likeness Detection tool to creators worldwide, giving them a way to find AI-generated videos that use their face without consent.
The checker sits in TikTok’s Transparency Centre and works without a TikTok account.
TikTok stamps its AI content with C2PA Content Credentials, but those can be stripped when a clip is downloaded or edited.
So the checker also hunts for VeraDura, TikTok’s own invisible watermark, which it says is far harder to remove.
Likeness Detection has been in testing with US creators since July.
The company says its systems have labelled over 5 billion AI-generated videos so far.
A reworked Manage Topics setting lets people choose how much AI-generated content turns up in their For You feed.

stories.title: OpenAI's chief scientist proposes an industry speed limit on AI measured by perplexity

articles.title: OpenAI's chief scientist has thoughts on how to limit AI development

facts.text: In this post, I argue for establishing perplexity (or, equivalently, cross-entropy loss) as a metric to compare between model developers and inform shared safety standards.
Perplexity measures how well a model predicts the next token on average; lower perplexity means better predictions.
GPT‑4, at ~0.91, was proficient at utilizing chain-of-thought reasoning productively
Now, as we have reached losses below 0.8, we have seen the emergence of transformative capabilities in fields like cybersecurity and mathematics.

I further propose common limits, based on perplexity and other measurements, that developers are committed to not crossing until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone
Publishing our internal perplexity measurements took some consideration; it gives competitors a clearer picture of where we stand
Pachocki’s post — described by Altman as “the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while”
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei then published a plan to “pace the frontier,” seemingly endorsed by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk.
Perplexity as a shared metric has challenges: Difficulty of comparison across labs.

stories.notes: Original company post read in full. Also in Reuters (Technology) and AI타임스, ZDNet Korea feeds. Pairs with Hendrycks pause story; pick only one. Strong evening-agnostic global story, morning slot fine.

articles.title: Anthropic researcher claims Riemann proof with Claude

facts.text: Mmathematician at Anthropic says he has used the company’s Claude AI model to prove the Riemann hypothesis (Levent Alpöge, note on his website on Friday, Bloomberg reported).
“I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Alpöge wrote.
The hypothesis, first proposed in 1859, concerns how prime numbers are spread out. It is one of the Clay Mathematics Institute’s seven Millennium Prize Problems, each of which carries a $1m prize.
The code runs to about 17 million lines, Science reported. (proof released in Lean)
Andrew Sutherland, a senior research scientist at MIT, told Bloomberg he had checked the code on his own computer.
Kevin Buzzard, a professor at Imperial College London, said nobody yet understands what the proof shows, Al Jazeera reported. The proof has not been formally accepted.
The claim came a day after the company’s record stock market debut.
In September, OpenAI said its models had produced a solution to the Navier-Stokes problem.

stories.notes: Secondhand (TNW citing Bloomberg, Science, SciAm, Al Jazeera). Must say 'claims'. Also covered by SCMP (200th birthday event in China, 16:01Z) and TechCrunch headline 'AI claimed a solution ... and a human did, too' - neither read. articles.title: OpenAI research agents cost $2,400 a day per researcher, report says

facts.text: OpenAI says its coding agents now complete 46% of research tasks that would take a person two to four hours, with no human help. In March the figure was 23%.
The figures come from Research acceleration: The jagged frontier, a report OpenAI published on Wednesday.
the median OpenAI researcher used about $2,400 of agent time a day in October. That is up 62% from $1,500 in September.
agent use per researcher rose elevenfold, from 0.5 to 5.7 “agent workdays” a day.
Agents succeeded alone 79% of the time when monitoring training runs ... They managed 25% when writing code for inference and serving systems
OpenAI flags a caveat in its own numbers. As agents improved, researchers may have changed which tasks they handed over
In a survey of 101 research staff ... The median answer was 40% of team headcount, or 30% of team compute.
OpenAI says labs should be required to track and publicly report signs of recursive self-improvement

articles.title: DealBook AGI panel: Dan Hendrycks wants frontier AI training paused

facts.text: Dan Hendrycks used the DealBook Summit to call for an indefinite pause on frontier AI training runs. Max Hodak, on the same panel, said enforcing one would take a surveillance state.
Hendrycks runs the Center for AI Safety
Hodak co-founded Neuralink and now runs Science Corporation.
“So now it’s, we’re going to need a more blunt intervention. That’s how it is,” Hendrycks said.
He described an indefinite pause on the biggest training runs, with carve-outs for narrow models such as DeepMind’s AlphaFold and voice models. Labs could still sell inference
“You’re setting up like an exhaustive surveillance state on the internet to enforce this,” Hodak said.
Staniszewski agreed a pause could work with global alignment, but said whether anyone can get it “is the big question mark”.
Hendrycks repeated the charges of the statement his group organised against the company [Anthropic]

facts.text: Etsy says it will revise its new terms of use. Longtime sellers had begun closing their shops over a clause that lets it use their work to train AI.
